speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. To investigate the cause of your anemia, have you noticed any dark, tarry stools, or have you been experiencing pain in your upper abdomen or black stools? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and reticulocyte count. REQUEST TEST: Stool occult blood.

text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue. I also have Appearance of pale skin, Presence of multiple pinpoint, red, nonblanching spots on extremities. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of non-blanching petechiae suggests a platelet disorder in addition to your anemia. REQUEST TEST: Platelet count and PT/PTT. REQUEST TEST: Peripheral blood smear. REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide images of the skin lesions and the blood smear.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 8.3 g/dL (low), WBC: 81,000 /mm3 (elevated), Platelets: 35,600 /mm3 (low); Peripheral Blood Smear Findings: Presence of immature cells with large, prominent nucleoli and pink, elongated, needle-shaped cytoplasmic inclusions.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Megakaryoblastic Leukemia. The combination of severe pancytopenia (anemia, thrombocytopenia), extreme leukocytosis with immature cells, and the pathognomonic Auer rods (needle-shaped cytoplasmic inclusions) on the blood smear confirms this diagnosis.
